page: OVHcloud l40s-180 is a GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-intensive workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 9124 processor with 30 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.75 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 180 GB of system memory, providing 6 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the server includes two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong performance characteristics. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests. The memory subsystem shows strong read-only bandwidth for small cached blocks, though large-block read and write speeds remain in the average tier. Notably, the dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs deliver top 10% performance in large language model inference speeds, processing prompts and generating text efficiently across small, medium, and large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by bundling dedicated compute cores, high-capacity GPU VRAM, and fast NVMe storage into a single KVM-virtualized instance. This hardware profile is highly suited for workloads such as large language model inference, machine learning training, data science pipelines, and high-performance computing tasks. It is also well-suited for database operations and multi-threaded decompression tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and hardware-accelerated instruction sets.
